about: Motet texts a Renaissance composer sets (the owner, 16 November 2026: "render 3 to 6 8-to-10-minute motets - you can download and choose the texts to set, based on Palestrina's corpus"): each a text Palestrina set as a motet, most in two parts (prima and secunda pars), as the liturgical books print it, accents kept (latin-text.js reads them; underlay.js lays them on the notes). Each part is a section of the piece, ended by its own final cadence; its phrases are the units of sense a point of imitation sets, divided at the books' punctuation and, within a long clause, where his settings begin a new point. How many points set each phrase is the composer's (mass-plan.js): his motets are not among the encodings measured here (Miller's are his masses), so their lengths by text are not measured.
source: The Divinum Officium project (github.com/DivinumOfficium/divinum-officium at d6c80662; MIT licence, Copyright (c) 2026 Divinum Officium; the trunk's research-downloads/liturgical-texts/divinum-officium), each text's file and lines under web/www named with it. Which book of his holds each setting is given from the standard work lists, not checked here against a catalogue.
metersFrom: The meters his masses' 1,318 movements are written in (Miller's encodings, measured on the trunk on 16 November 2026 by research/renaissance-mass/all-meters.mjs): what a motet's meter is drawn from until his motets are measured. The 114 in 3/2 left out of a motet's draw (16 November 2026; the owner, of the selection's Sicut cervus, sung whole in 3/2: "Intuitively, Sicut Cervus seemed rushed to me"; "make sure the tempi are realistic"): they are the masses' triple sections, and in his time a ternary passage stood within a binary piece -- "After c. 1520 binary signatures became standard for most pieces, and ternary passages within them were notated as sesquialtera or triple proportions" (S. A. Kingsbury 2002, Choral Journal 42(9), after DeFord and Apel) -- so that a whole motet in sesquialtera, three minims to every tactus, is none of his. Drawn binary until the composer sets a ternary passage within a binary piece; a Mass's sections keep their own (mass-ordinary.json).

sicut-cervus.title: Sicut cervus
sicut-cervus.set: Palestrina, for four voices, with its second part Sitivit anima mea (his second book of motets for four voices). Psalm 41:2-4, the tract of the Easter Vigil; his motet reads "ad Deum fortem vivum" and "quotidie" where the tract as printed here reads "ad Deum vivum" and "per singulos dies".

sections.name: Sitivit anima mea
phrases: dum dícitur mihi per síngulos dies:

salve-regina.title: Salve Regina
salve-regina.set: Palestrina, several settings (for four, five, six, eight and twelve voices). The Marian antiphon from Trinity to Advent, in two parts as his settings divide it, the second begun at "Eja ergo".

sections.name: Eja ergo
phrases: Et Jesum, benedíctum fructum ventris tui,

tu-es-petrus.title: Tu es Petrus
tu-es-petrus.set: Palestrina, for six voices, with its second part Quodcumque ligaveris (and a setting for seven). Matthew 16:18-19, the responsory of Saints Peter and Paul: both parts end with its refrain, "et tibi dabo claves regni caelorum".

o-magnum-mysterium.title: O magnum mysterium
o-magnum-mysterium.set: Palestrina, for six voices, with its second part Quem vidistis pastores. Two responsories of Christmas Matins, both parts ended by the same refrain and Alleluia.

cum-complerentur.title: Cum complerentur
cum-complerentur.set: Palestrina, for six voices, as Dum complerentur, with its second part Dum ergo essent. Acts 2:1-2, the responsory of Pentecost as printed here ("Cum complerentur ... in eodem loco"); his motet's first words are the antiphon's, "Dum complerentur dies Pentecostes, erant omnes pariter dicentes".

viri-galilaei.title: Viri Galilaei
viri-galilaei.set: Palestrina, for six voices, with its second part Ascendit Deus. Acts 1:11 and Psalms 46:6 and 102:19, of the Ascension; each of its three sentences ends with an Alleluia, as the Office's and the Mass's print the second and third.
viri-galilaei.from: horas/Latin/Tempora/Pasc5-4.txt, line 321 (Viri Galilaei) and line 157 (Dominus in caelo); missa/Latin/Tempora/Pasc5-4.txt, line 53 (Ascendit Deus, the Offertory)
